verdict_A_user_outcome.source_evidence: The App header mounts one SiteAccessControl beside UserMenu across Prepare and SEO. Its temporary toolbar guidance remains visible after Deny, a direct click requests only the captured HTTP(S) origin, and a separate click reloads the captured tab. Prepare's page-key and run-sequence guard clears the old pending run on navigation; SEO's page-key and audit-run guards restart on the fresh document and ignore old results. No persistent-permission denial inference, automatic request, reload, or retry is present.
verdict_A_user_outcome.remaining: The new product control and Chrome's native permission prompt have not yet been observed together in a built extension. The existing native clicked-button evidence establishes that an awaited tabs.query/getFrame sequence preserves the request gesture in Chrome 149, but its button was ephemeral test UI. Native product acceptance remains necessary to close the user outcome.

findings.evidence: Both action handlers await verifyLiveSiteAccessTarget immediately before requesting or reloading. It compares captured tab ID and URL with Chrome's active tab, top-frame document ID and URL, then checks the active tab again. Source tests change browser state before React publishes it and replace the same-URL document; both reject request and reload. The native awaited-gesture probe supports this order in Chrome 149.

sessionSeq advances on every open/close and captured-page change. Both async action paths check the captured session after live verification and before publishing the result. Delayed Allow and Deny tests close/reopen the control, and navigation tests reject a late grant.

The new connected SEO test mounts the shared control beside SeoView, explicitly reloads the captured page, fires a new document ID, and observes a further capture call without requesting persistent access. SeoView's independent navigation tests prove old-result rejection and fresh-document audit behavior.
findings.limit: The connected reload test asserts only a capture call count, not the resulting fresh audit's displayed content; its claim of a fresh successful audit relies on the adjacent SEO navigation tests and source guards.

verdict_B_engineering_contract.new_material_breakage: None identified in source review. The live read still has the ordinary asynchronous browser-state race after its final check; no atomic Chrome compare-and-reload API is available in this implementation, and this does not recreate the reported last-render identity defect.

verification_scope: Read-only source, diff, contract, and test-evidence review. No heavy build, browser run, or product edit; CI/import and native product acceptance belong to separate active lanes.
